item: The swap window's cleanup passes one section of the state lock, so a failed exit of it no longer blocks the cleanup with the window held
refs: coordinator 17 Oct (option 2 on the _revive/_close_window plan); finding F3 of the independent read of PR #1435; independent read of PR #1442; PR #1442
summary: swap_window's cleanup passed three with-_STATE sections (the _DISK_CHANGED read, _revive, _close_window), so a failed exit of the first or the second (a plain lock left held; measured with the allocator on cold free lists, 3.13) blocked the next section of the SAME cleanup with the exclusive library window held and every new pooled connection waiting. They are now one section in _close_window(swapped, earlier=None); _revive is gone. A failed exit of that one still raises the error and the finally still gives the window back, the pool serves again, but _STATE stays held and the NEXT swap blocks at its first section and stops the pool again as before. The sections before the close are the same exits and still block this swap's close: 4 of 5 for a swap that changes the disk (reset, bump, open, disk_changing in the body; every restore, repair and encrypt), 3 of 4 for one refused before disk_changing, from 5 of 6 on both. Merging the opening sections would cut the sites, not remove the block; only dropping _STATE does (a separate change, after its proof). Said in swap_window's docstring and pinned by four tests (one per section before the close) and a count (3 opening, 1 disk_changing, 1 cleanup) followed through helpers to any depth. Also closes a path the old sweep could not see: a failure before the cleanup's read of _DISK_CHANGED left the window's own connections valid again after disk_changing (reproduced on main's module; pinned with its red-without). Red-without: the section count (1; 3 on the module rewritten back) and a stand-in _STATE whose exit fails and stays held (old shape: blocked, window held; new: MemoryError, window given back, a connecting() gets through). Not here: dropping _STATE.
